rows: Company/flag-state and MLC minimum standards apply; potable water production/storage capacity is vessel-specific — follow ship's SMS and MLC Title 3 catering standards

tables.name: MLC 2006 Title 3 — Food & Catering Highlights
rows: Food must be of appropriate quality, nutritional value, and sufficient quantity for the voyage, taking into account crew number, religious/cultural requirements and length of voyage
Food and drinking water must be provided to seafarers at no cost during their period of engagement
Ships with a prescribed manning complement must carry a qualified ship's cook, trained and certified per flag State requirements
Food and catering, and galley hygiene, are subject to frequent inspection as part of shipboard MLC/ISM routines and are checked during PSC and flag inspections

tables.name: Galley Fire & Safety Checklist Themes
rows: Keep exhaust hood/ducting grease-free, deep fat fryers fitted with high-temp cut-out, galley fire blanket and appropriate extinguisher (Class F/K for cooking oil fires) readily accessible
All equipment, crockery storage and loose items secured/latched before getting underway or in heavy weather
Regular inspection of gas connections (LPG lockers vented overboard, remote shut-off) and electrical appliance earthing/RCD protection
Colour-coded chopping boards, separate raw/cooked storage, hand-washing stations, pest control programme
